samples.summary: The new loopback `armLaunch` redirect may make every CLI login look cross-site to the out-of-diff `assertCliStartNotCrossSite` guard
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:351` now hands the opener `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/launch/<token>`, which 302s to `<server>/auth/github?mode=cli…` (`login.ts:826`, `login.ts:654-668`). The backend refuses a `?mode=cli` start whose `Sec-Fetch-Site` is `cross-site`: `packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:301-311` (`ALLOWED_FETCH_SITES` = none/same-origin/same-site). Before this change the opener navigated straight to the server origin, so the header was `none`. With a loopback→server redirect in the chain, browsers that recompute `Sec-Fetch-Site` across a cross-site redirect will send `cross-site`, and `wafflebase login` would 400 on every real (non-loopback-server) deployment. Nothing in the repo tests the redirect-chain header value — `github-auth.guard.spec.ts:254` only feeds the header directly. To confirm: a real Chrome/Firefox run through `/launch/<token>` against a non-loopback backend, or a citation of the Fetch Metadata `none`-is-sticky-across-redirects behaviour.

samples.summary: Three error emitters were left un-attributed while every sibling gained `command`
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:85` (`ctx list`), `packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:69` (`status`) and `packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:139` (`sheets cells batch`, the malformed-JSON path) still call `outputError(e)` with no acting command, while every other action in the same packages now passes `this`. docs/design/cli.md:1493 documents the envelope as carrying `command`, so an agent branching on attribution gets it for `sheets cells get` but not for `sheets cells batch`'s parse failure or for the two session commands.

samples.summary: Out-of-diff docs still describe the pre-change cookie names and the old `?confirm=` contract
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/README.md:447` says tokens are set as cookies named `wafflebase_session` / `wafflebase_refresh`, with no mention of the `__Host-` prefix the change now applies (`oauth-state.ts:89-95`); `packages/backend/README.md:456` still says the click "carries the `__Host-wafflebase_cli_confirm` cookie secret back as `?confirm=`", but `?confirm=` is now `cliConfirmToken(secret, port, nonce, challenge)` (`cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:97-107`). `docs/design/rest-api.md:118` likewise says `JwtStrategy` accepts JWTs from the `wafflebase_session` cookie, whereas `jwt.strategy.ts:19` now reads only `sessionCookieName()`. (docs/design/backend.md and docs/design/cli.md were updated; these three were not.)

samples.summary: e2e helpers hardcode the bare `wafflebase_session` cookie name, which is now environment-dependent
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/test/authenticated-http.e2e-spec.ts:48` (and the same helper in notification/user-doc-styles/api-key-http/document-file-serving/folder e2e specs) builds `wafflebase_session=${token}`. `jwt.strategy.ts:19` now resolves the name through `sessionCookieName()`, which returns `__Host-wafflebase_session` whenever `COOKIE_SECURE=true` or `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` is `https://`. The integration helper only defaults the callback URL with `??=` (`packages/backend/test/helpers/integration-helpers.ts:93`), so any environment that already exports an https callback URL or `COOKIE_SECURE=true` silently unauthenticates the whole integration lane.

samples.summary: Two new login tests drive `announceLoginUrl` without isolating `WAFFLEBASE_CONFIG`, so they write into the real `~/.wafflebase`
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:352` and `:429` set only `WAFFLEBASE_SESSION`; the first test at `:267-268` sets `WAFFLEBASE_CONFIG` and the shared `afterEach` deletes it (`:261`). `announceLoginUrl` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:152) resolves `join(dirname(getConfigPath()), 'login-url.txt')`, and `getConfigPath()` falls back to `~/.wafflebase/config.yaml` — also invoking `migrateConfigIfNeeded`, which copies the developer's real config. These two runs therefore create (and delete) a file in the user's real config directory.

finding.summary: The new loopback `armLaunch` redirect may make every CLI login look cross-site to the out-of-diff `assertCliStartNotCrossSite` guard
finding.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:351` now hands the opener `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/launch/<token>`, which 302s to `<server>/auth/github?mode=cli…` (`login.ts:826`, `login.ts:654-668`). The backend refuses a `?mode=cli` start whose `Sec-Fetch-Site` is `cross-site`: `packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:301-311` (`ALLOWED_FETCH_SITES` = none/same-origin/same-site). Before this change the opener navigated straight to the server origin, so the header was `none`. With a loopback→server redirect in the chain, browsers that recompute `Sec-Fetch-Site` across a cross-site redirect will send `cross-site`, and `wafflebase login` would 400 on every real (non-loopback-server) deployment. Nothing in the repo tests the redirect-chain header value — `github-auth.guard.spec.ts:254` only feeds the header directly. To confirm: a real Chrome/Firefox run through `/launch/<token>` against a non-loopback backend, or a citation of the Fetch Metadata `none`-is-sticky-across-redirects behaviour.

verdict.reason: The redirect-chain request never reaches the guard's cross-site check. CliLoginConfirmMiddleware is registered ahead of the guard on GET auth/github (auth.module.ts:45-49; controller prefix 'auth', no global prefix in main.ts) and short-circuits every unconfirmed ?mode=cli start with a 200 confirmation page, without calling next() (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:112-171, esp. 162-170; pinned by cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts:44-47). So whatever Sec-Fetch-Site a browser computes for the 127.0.0.1/launch -> server 302 (login.ts:654-669, 826-829) is consumed by the middleware, not by assertCliStartNotCrossSite (github-auth.guard.ts:301-311). The only request that reaches the guard is the click on the confirmation page, whose href is the relative /auth/github?...&confirm=... on the backend's own origin (middleware.ts:193-197, 234) => same-origin, which is in ALLOWED_FETCH_SITES (github-auth.guard.ts:122). The guard only sees a CLI start directly when the middleware falls through: !cliLoginAvailable() (middleware.ts:121-123), where the login is refused anyway by assertCliLoginAvailable (guard.ts:232-244) so at most the 400 wording differs, or an unusable port (middleware.ts:128-132), which a real CLI start never produces (login.ts:344). Hence the predicted 'wafflebase login 400s on every non-loopback deployment' cannot occur.

finding.summary: Logout's `clearCookie` now inherits `COOKIE_SECURE`, so `COOKIE_SECURE=true` on an origin actually served over http leaves the session cookie in the browser at sign-out
finding.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:474-476 clears `wafflebase_session`/`wafflebase_refresh` with `this.baseCookieOptions()`, whose `secure` is now `secureCookies()` and therefore operator-settable. A `Set-Cookie` carrying `Secure` sent from a plain-http origin is dropped by the browser, so the expiring cookie never lands and the previously-set session cookie survives logout. The pre-delta derivation could only produce `secure: true` on an origin that had declared itself https; the new override can produce it on an origin that is not. Same class as the `Secure`-on-http dead-login the PR describes, but on the revocation path rather than the login path, so it fails quietly instead of loudly.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that logout clears the session cookies with `this.baseCookieOptions()` whose `secure` comes from `useSecureCookies()`/`COOKIE_SECURE`, so a `Secure` expiry sent from a plain-http origin is dropped and the session survives sign-out. The code does not do that. `clearAuthCookies` (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:349-361) spreads the base options and then explicitly overrides `secure` on each iteration: `for (const secure of [true, false]) res.clearCookie(name, { ...base, secure })`, over a name set of the (possibly `__Host-` prefixed) session/refresh names plus `UNPREFIXED_SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES` (oauth-state.ts:104-107). So the non-`Secure` expiry — the one that can arrive over http — is always emitted regardless of `COOKIE_SECURE`. The rationale is documented at auth.controller.ts:325-348 and pinned by tests at auth.controller.spec.ts:616-636 (asserts both `name:true` and `name:false` for `__Host-wafflebase_session/refresh` and the bare names) and :638-647 (exactly 4 clearCookie calls in development). The cited evidence location (474-476) does not exist; the file is 415 lines. `clearAuthCookies` is the only path clearing session/refresh cookies (called at :88 logout, :275, :286, :302 refresh); the other `clearCookie` calls at :162 and :182 are OAuth/CLI state cookies. Ground: not-present.
